transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I guess… my sleep’s been really messed up. I work overnights, and even when I get off, I just lie there awake. Then if I do fall asleep, I wake up scared, like I didn’t really rest at all.
Even when you do manage to sleep, do you still feel tired or unrefreshed during the day?
Yeah… even if I sleep, it doesn’t feel like I did. I wake up scared, and I’m still tired, like I never really rested.
Do you usually have trouble falling asleep, or does it happen pretty quickly once you lie down?
It’s mostly… I can’t fall asleep. I’ll get off work and lie there wide awake for a long time. Then if I finally drift off, I wake up scared, and it doesn’t feel like I rested.
When you wake up scared during the night, do you remember having a bad dream or feeling afraid while you were asleep?
I don’t always remember a dream… I just wake up scared. Like I wasn’t really asleep right, and I still feel worn out.
When you're trying to fall asleep, how long does it usually take you to actually fall asleep?
A long time… usually. I don’t really keep track, but after I get off my overnight shift I’ll just lay there wide awake for hours sometimes before I drift off.
How often do you wake up during the night after you've fallen asleep?
A lot… I don’t really count it. When I do finally fall asleep, I’ll wake up scared, and then it feels like I never really rested.
Even when you do sleep, do you feel drowsy or have trouble staying alert during the day?
Yeah… I feel worn out, like I never really slept. Even when I do doze off, it’s all broken up, so during the day I’m just… tired and not really alert.
When you finally do fall asleep, does it feel like you’re sleeping during the wrong part of your body’s natural sleep cycle, like you’re forcing yourself to sleep when your body isn’t ready?

I don’t know if it’s like… my natural cycle or whatever. I just know after my overnight shift, I’m exhausted but I still lie there awake, and then when I finally sleep it’s broken up. I wake up scared and don’t feel rested.
During the day, do you ever fall asleep unintentionally or feel an overwhelming need to sleep, even if you managed to get some rest?
Yeah… sometimes it just hits me during the day. Even if I slept a little, it doesn’t feel like real sleep. I’m just worn out from being awake after my shift and waking up scared.

When you have trouble sleeping after your overnight shift, does it usually take you a long time to fall asleep at the beginning of your sleep period, or do you fall asleep okay but then wake up multiple times during your sleep?

It’s… kind of both. After my overnight shift I’ll be exhausted, but I still just lie there awake for a long time. Then when I finally do fall asleep, I keep waking up… scared, and it doesn’t feel like I rested.
When you wake up scared during the night, do you ever have vivid dreams or nightmares, or find yourself acting out your dreams while asleep?
I don’t really know about vivid dreams or acting anything out. I just… wake up scared after I finally fall asleep, and it feels like I didn’t really rest.
Have you ever felt like you're awake but can't move your body when you're falling asleep or just waking up?
I don’t know… I don’t think it’s like I can’t move. It’s more that my sleep is just broken up. I get off work and I’m wide awake, then when I finally sleep I wake up scared and still feel exhausted.
Have you ever experienced a moment where you felt awake but couldn't move your body, either when you were falling asleep or just waking up?
I… I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed being awake and unable to move.
Do you ever feel an uncomfortable urge to move your legs, especially when you're trying to fall asleep or while you're resting?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed anything like needing to move my legs.
Have you ever felt sudden muscle weakness or felt like your body gave out while you were awake, especially during the day when you're tired?
No… I don’t think my body gives out like that. I get tired, but I haven’t noticed sudden weakness.
Do you find that your sleep problems improve when you're not working overnight shifts, or when you're able to sleep at night instead of during the day?
Not really… even after I get off overnight, I’ll lie there wide awake. And if I do fall asleep, I wake up scared… like I didn’t rest at all.
Have you ever felt like you were awake but couldn't move your body when you were falling asleep or just waking up?
Not that I can tell… I just know my sleep’s been really broken. I’ll get off overnight and still be wide awake, and when I do fall asleep I wake up scared, like I didn’t rest at all.
Do you find that your sleep improves when you're able to maintain a consistent sleep schedule that aligns with your usual body clock, rather than trying to sleep at different times?
No… not really. Even when I’m supposed to sleep after work, I just lay there awake. And if I do fall asleep, I wake up scared… like I didn’t rest at all.
Have you ever felt like you were awake but couldn't move your body when falling asleep or just waking up?
I don’t think so… I mean, I haven’t noticed being stuck like that. It’s more just… bad sleep.
